# KBD Constraints — Prior Authorization Workbench

These constraints are derived from the repository documentation and its Rust,
React/Vite, Tauri, and Flutter architecture. KBD and every executing tool must
apply them before a change can be archived.

## Blocking Constraints

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: build-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: "All build-only surfaces must compile or analyze successfully"
    command: "cargo build --workspace && pnpm --dir web build && flutter analyze mobile"

  - id: invariant-tests-pass
    severity: blocking
    description: "Rust domain invariants and Flutter tests must pass"
    command: "cargo test --workspace && flutter test mobile"

  - id: architecture-audit-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: "The repository architecture audit must pass"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: three-evidence-states
    severity: blocking
    description: "Evidence state must preserve met, gap, and void as distinct values"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: clinical-authority-boundary
    severity: blocking
    description: "Administrative authority must never imply permission to affirm a clinical gate or sign a letter"
    command: "cargo test --workspace"

  - id: host-remains-shell-neutral
    severity: blocking
    description: "aso-host must not depend on Axum, Tauri, Flutter, or another presentation shell"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: no-query-cache
    severity: blocking
    description: "Do not add a query-cache dependency; the entity graph owns freshness"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: generated-theme-is-read-only
    severity: blocking
    description: "Do not hand-edit web/src/theme.css or mobile/lib/core/theme/tokens.dart; edit tokens.toml and regenerate"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh"

  - id: no-console-log-in-web-source
    severity: blocking
    description: "No console.log statements in web TypeScript source"
    check: "rg -n 'console\\.log' web/src -g '*.ts' -g '*.tsx'"

  - id: no-any-type-in-web-source
    severity: blocking
    description: "No explicit any type in web TypeScript source"
    check: "rg -n ': any([,;)>]|$)' web/src -g '*.ts' -g '*.tsx'"

  - id: no-hardcoded-secrets
    severity: blocking
    description: "No hardcoded API keys, tokens, or passwords in application source"
    check: "rg -n 'sk-|api_key|API_KEY|secret.*=[[:space:]]*[\"'\"'][A-Za-z0-9]' crates web/src mobile/lib desktop/src-tauri/src"
```

## Warning Constraints

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: tests-for-new-features
    severity: warning
    description: "Tests exist for every new behavior introduced by a change"

  - id: lint-clean
    severity: warning
    description: "Architecture, Rust, web, and Flutter lint checks pass without warnings"
    command: "bash scripts/audit.sh && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets && pnpm --dir web lint && flutter analyze mobile"

  - id: no-stub-comments
    severity: warning
    description: "No TODO, FIXME, STUB, or HACK comments are introduced"
    check: "rg -n 'TODO|FIXME|STUB|HACK' crates web/src mobile/lib desktop/src-tauri/src"

  - id: accessibility-basics
    severity: warning
    description: "New UI uses semantic HTML/widgets, keyboard access, labels, and visible focus states"
    note: "Manual review is required"

  - id: exact-dependency-pins
    severity: warning
    description: "Preserve exact pins for code-generation and FFI dependency graphs unless the full coherent set is validated"
```

## Workflow Triggers

```yaml
workflow_triggers:
  - event: on_iteration_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: "cargo build --workspace && pnpm --dir web build && flutter analyze mobile"

  - event: on_change_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: "cargo test --workspace && flutter test mobile"
```

## Project Notes

- The focus project is the repository root; no multi-root VS Code workspace was found.
- `web/openspec/config.yaml` is nested below the focus root and has no specs, so KBD uses its built-in change management until a root OpenSpec project or actual specs are added.
- Design intent comes from `docs/design/`; sequencing comes from `docs/plan/build-order.md`; architecture decisions come from `docs/architecture/`.
acceptance_criteria:
## 1. Eligibility and implementation

- [x] 1.1 Confirm dependency completion, assigned file ownership, frozen web-00 contracts, and applicable decision gates before edits; verify canonical KBD/OpenSpec state and retain the result.
- [x] 1.2 Add the additive case-command migration and least-privilege functions; verify fresh/upgrade schema checks and direct-write refusal.
- [x] 1.3 Implement the shell-neutral case aggregate/service and PostgreSQL adapter; verify idempotent create, detail, update, transition, lost-response, and conflict tests.
- [x] 1.4 Mount typed browser HTTP routes; verify equivalent success/error/refusal contract tests without a native implementation claim.

## 2. Focused verification

- [ ] 2.1 Run focused T0/T1 plus authority/tenant sabotage-and-restore, artifact-refiner, and adversarial review.

## 3. Completion evidence

- [ ] 3.1 Record actual commands and observed outputs, confirm real mounted callers at this change boundary, update documentation/spec deltas, and mark only satisfied work complete.
## Why

The web application cannot perform its central case-to-letter workflow. Persist verified, idempotent case creation and management commands through typed browser HTTP routes.

## What Changes

- Persist verified, idempotent case creation and management commands through typed browser HTTP routes.
- Preserve verified tenant scope, three evidence states, clinical authority, source citations, no query cache, and shell-neutral application services.
- Use the browser and its mounted HTTP routes as the only behavioral acceptance surface in this child. Typed Tauri wrappers are deferred to RA19/RA21 after web-17 passes.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `case-command-core`: Persist verified, idempotent case creation and management commands through typed browser HTTP routes.

### Modified Capabilities

None.

## Impact

This ordered web-first change belongs to `runtime-architecture › web-case-to-letter` and follows the reviewed child plan. It may affect the exact schema, host, server, projection, or React surfaces named by that plan; implementation is not authorized by this planning artifact alone.


--- openspec/changes/web-01-case-command-core/design.md ---
## Context

This is ordered change `web-01-case-command-core` in the reviewed `runtime-architecture › web-case-to-letter` plan. The repository already provides verified sessions, clinical command patterns, authorized projection, PGlite/PEM materialization, and responsive React foundations, but this capability is absent or incomplete.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:** Implement only `case-command-core` at its focused contract boundary and retain shell-neutral `AppServices`, verified tenant scope, typed browser HTTP contracts, and explicit replica privacy classification before publication.

**Non-Goals:** No typed Tauri wrappers, Tauri runtime certification, native SQLite selection, Flutter/mobile work, real payer transport, external inference, production deployment, or broad child integration run. Native delivery resumes only after web-17 passes.

## Decisions

- Follow the frozen decisions and dependency order in the child plan; do not reopen them during apply.
- Use additive migrations and least-privilege security-definer functions for durable effects; direct production-role table writes remain refused.
- Keep durable domain state in Postgres/PEM and transient view state in scoped Zustand.
- Add document/page/date to every generated external assertion. Documentless annotations or criteria may guide work but cannot become an included assertion.
- Run only applicable Tier 0 and focused Tier 1 checks in this change. Child Tier 2 belongs to web-17.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Service/HTTP drift] → Keep browser HTTP command contracts beside the shell-neutral service and verify equivalent refusal semantics.
- [Replica disclosure] → Require the plan's lane/privacy/column/tenant/revocation record before any new publication.
- [False readiness] → Acceptance names only the mounted boundary completed by this change and does not reuse fixture-only evidence as product evidence.

## Migration Plan

Apply additive schema and contract changes before enabling their callers. Preserve existing reads until the focused migration is verified. Roll back callers first; never delete historical clinical or audit records as rollback.


--- openspec/changes/web-01-case-command-core/specs/case-command-core/spec.md ---
## Purpose

Defines the observable behavior required for verified case commands in the web-first case-to-letter workflow.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Verified case commands
The system SHALL satisfy this capability under verified tenant scope while preserving clinical authority, citation, privacy, and no-query-cache invariants.

#### Scenario: Required behavior
- **WHEN** an authenticated coordinator creates or updates a case with a stable command ID
- **THEN** one tenant-scoped result commits and retry reconciles while forged or foreign scope is refused

#### Scenario: Scope or authority refusal
- **WHEN** the caller is unauthenticated, foreign to the practice, stale, or lacks the capability required by this operation
- **THEN** the system refuses the operation without publishing protected data or committing a partial effect

findings.claim: The mounted case HTTP routes do not enforce the required case capabilities before executing reads or mutations.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion/spec says callers that lack the capability required by the operation must be refused; `clinical_context(&state, &headers, query.practice_id)` returns `(context, _)` and every handler discards capabilities, then directly calls `state.services.create_case/list_cases/read_case/update_case/transition_case`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the capabilities returned by `clinical_context` in each handler and require `case:read` for reads and `case_write` for create/update/transition/command reconciliation before calling AppServices.

findings.claim: The shell-neutral case service authorizes every human user without checking operation-specific case capabilities.
findings.evidence: `check_case_context` only rejects expired sessions and non-`Principal::User`, while the spec requires refusal when a caller "lacks the capability required by this operation".
findings.suggested_fix: Carry verified capabilities into the service boundary or add an authority/capability port check for `case:read` and `case_write` before delegating to the repository.

findings.claim: The migration uses the PostgreSQL 17 `MAINTAIN` privilege unconditionally, which can fail on older supported PostgreSQL versions.
findings.evidence: The migration calls `pg_catalog.has_table_privilege(..., 'SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER, MAINTAIN')`, while the Rust role checks in `crates/aso-web-server/src/adapters/gate.rs` explicitly guard `MAINTAIN` with `current_setting('server_version_num')::integer >= 170000`, showing compatibility is expected.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the `MAINTAIN` check behind a server-version guard in the migration, matching the Rust `ROLE_CHECK`/`CASE_ROLE_CHECK` pattern.

findings.claim: The existing `/api/cases/{case_id}/evidence` evidence-count route is removed from this router without an equivalent replacement in the shown diff.
findings.evidence: The deleted code routed `Router::new().route("/api/cases/{case_id}/evidence", get(evidence_counts))` and serialized distinct `met`, `gap`, and `void` counts; the new router only mounts `/api/cases`, `/api/cases/{case_id}`, `/api/cases/{case_id}/status`, and command lookup routes, while the blocking constraint requires preserving three evidence states.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the evidence-count route or show/move an equivalent mounted route that still returns distinct `met`, `gap`, and `void` values.

findings.claim: The internal gate denies write-only case callers even though the write routes themselves require only `case_write`.
findings.evidence: The case policy first accepts `CaseResource { write: true }` with `required = "case_write"`, but then unconditionally calls `state.services.read_case(&context, &capabilities, case_id)`, and `AppServices::read_case` in `crates/aso-host/src/case_management.rs` requires `"case:read"`; acceptance requires refusal only when the caller lacks the capability required by this operation.
findings.suggested_fix: For write case resources, validate case existence/scope through a repository/service path that requires `case_write`, or add a dedicated `require_case_access(context, capabilities, case_id, required_capability)` check instead of calling the read endpoint.

finding_resolution.finding: Route and service capability checks missing.
Write policy incorrectly also required case:read.
finding_resolution.resolution: Fixed: Gate uses authorize_case_write_target for write resources and read_case only for reads. A write-only policy case passes; the same principal read is denied.
Not applicable to the explicit PostgreSQL 18 deployment.
No mounted behavior existed in HEAD; retaining it would newly expose an unauthenticated route. Evidence publication is assigned to web-08/web-09.
